title: The Millennium Bet
story: January 2000 was the height of the dot-com mania. Within two years Wipro had lost 42% and HCL Technologies 64%. Reliance compounded about 15x by 2008 despite the Ambani brothers' split, ITC rose almost 5x, and gold began a decade-long bull run from near a 20-year low. Patient HCL holders were finally rewarded after 2008, with about 17x more by 2026.

headlines.text: Three new states are carved out of Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Delhi's first Metro line opens to the public between Shahdara and Tis Hazari
India's largest software company makes its stock market debut
A visiting US President agrees a plan to separate India's civilian and military nuclear sites

title: The Commodity Supercycle
story: China's building boom lifted metals and oil from 2003, and India's state-owned industrials went with it: SAIL rose 6x in two years and BHEL about 27x by 2011. Crude hit $147 a barrel in July 2008 and fell below $40 by December. After 2011 the party was over for steel: SAIL is lower today than in January 2011, while silver went on to multiply about 4x.

headlines.text: The Prime Minister announces India will send an unmanned mission to the Moon
Parliament passes a law giving citizens the right to demand information from the government
An Indian steelmaker wins a bidding war for Anglo-Dutch Corus
A film set in Mumbai's slums wins eight Oscars, two of them for A. R. Rahman

title: Open Road
story: India's car and truck boom: Maruti Suzuki rose 2.5x in eight years and MRF nearly 3x, while crude oil quadrupled. The bigger money came after 2012. MRF climbed another 18x to become India's most expensive share, and Maruti and Ashok Leyland gained 14-15x. ONGC, the oil producer, barely moved.

headlines.text: India's cricketers tour Pakistan for a full series for the first time in 14 years
India plays its first-ever Twenty20 international, in Johannesburg
A car priced at one lakh rupees is unveiled at the Delhi Auto Expo
The first 12-digit unique identity numbers are handed out in a Maharashtra village

title: Boom, Bust, Repeat
story: 2007 was the top of India's great bull run. Suzlon, Unitech and Reliance Communications were the darlings; by 2015 they had lost 82-95% of their value, and Unitech's promoters later went to jail. ICICI Bank halved in the 2008 crash and recovered. TCS fell 60% and then rose about 10x from the bottom. Crude touched $147 in July 2008 before collapsing.

headlines.text: A British telecom giant pays over $10 billion for control of Hutchison Essar
India's first lunar probe helps find evidence of water on the Moon
Treasure worth over a lakh crore rupees is found in the vaults of a Kerala temple
The Supreme Court gives voters a 'None of the Above' button

title: The Biggest IPO Ever
story: Reliance Power's February 2008 IPO was oversubscribed about 70 times, then closed below its issue price on listing day. You arrived a month later. By 2016 it had lost 82% and DLF 86%. Reliance Industries went nowhere for eight years, then rose about 6x by 2026 on Jio and retail. Gold doubled, and crude ended below where you started.

headlines.text: An Indian carmaker agrees to buy Jaguar and Land Rover from Ford
The first double century in men's one-day international cricket is scored
Regulators suspend the flying licence of a liquor baron's airline
An Indian e-commerce startup raises $1 billion in a single funding round

title: The Telecom Wars
story: Right after the 2008 crash, a dozen operators were fighting a tariff war. Reliance Communications lost 86% by 2017 and later went bankrupt. Idea did well until Jio arrived in late 2016, then lost most of its value. Bharti Airtel went sideways for eight years before rising about 7.5x. The quiet winner was TCS, up 9.5x.

headlines.text: A former Infosys CEO is picked to lead a new national identity authority
A 73-year-old activist's hunger strike for an anti-corruption ombudsman draws huge crowds
Sachin Tendulkar plays his 200th and final Test match
The Planning Commission is replaced by a new policy think tank

title: Scam Season
story: 2010 brought the 2G spectrum and Commonwealth Games scandals. Unitech, whose managing director was arrested in the 2G case, lost 86% by 2018. HCC, the builder behind Lavasa, lost 44%, and Hindustan Copper fell 73% after a speculative frenzy. Silver nearly doubled to its 2011 peak and then gave most of it back. Bharti Airtel was the steady survivor.

headlines.text: The government auctions 3G mobile airwaves for the first time
Two regional power grids collapse, leaving over 600 million people without electricity
India's Mars orbiter reaches Mars on its first attempt
Parliament passes a constitutional amendment to create a single nationwide sales tax

title: Credit Where It's Due
story: Bajaj Finance turned loans for fridges and phones into one of India's greatest wealth creators: about 61x in eight years and about 179x by 2026. Royal Enfield's revival took Eicher Motors up 15x. Infosys doubled and SBI rose 49%, while crude crashed from over $100 to under $50 in 2014-15.

headlines.text: A former telecom minister is arrested over the allocation of 2G spectrum
India launches its first mission to Mars
A popular instant noodle brand is banned by the food regulator
Apple begins assembling iPhones at a plant in Bengaluru

title: Banking on Growth
story: Yes Bank was India's fastest-growing bank and rose almost 7x in six years. Then it collapsed: by January 2020 it was back where you started, and an RBI rescue followed in March. Kotak and HDFC Bank compounded 6-8x. Punjab National Bank lost 58% as bad loans and the Nirav Modi fraud came to light.

headlines.text: WHO removes India from its list of countries where polio is endemic
The government launches a campaign to turn India into a global manufacturing hub
An Indian shuttler wins Olympic silver in Rio
An American retail giant buys a controlling stake in India's biggest e-commerce company

title: Premium India
story: The brands India's new middle class paid up for. Page Industries (Jockey) rose 7x, Asian Paints and Titan more than 4x, and Jubilant FoodWorks (Domino's) nearly 3x. Crude lost 44% over the same eight years, and gold did little until 2019.

headlines.text: Saina Nehwal wins India's first Olympic medal in badminton
A nationwide cleanliness campaign is launched on Gandhi Jayanti
The Supreme Court bans liquor sales within 500 metres of highways
Kerala is hit by its worst floods in nearly a century

title: The Taper Tantrum
story: In mid-2013 the US Federal Reserve hinted it would slow its bond buying, and the rupee fell to a record low near 69 to the dollar. Sun Pharma more than doubled in two years, then lost almost half amid its Ranbaxy merger and US regulator trouble. Hindustan Unilever and Infosys each rose over 4x, while SBI barely moved in eight years.

headlines.text: India takes delivery of a refitted Soviet-era aircraft carrier from Russia
The Supreme Court strikes down a law used to arrest people over online posts
A new nationwide tax is launched at a midnight session of Parliament
India's lunar lander loses contact moments before touchdown

title: All That Glitters
story: PC Jeweller rose about 11x by January 2018, then lost 95% in two years amid governance concerns in the wake of the Nirav Modi scandal. Titan (Tanishq) and gold-loan lender Muthoot Finance compounded 11-14x. Gold and silver did little until 2019 and then took off.

headlines.text: An Indian-born engineer is named CEO of Microsoft
A liquor baron leaves India as banks chase about Rs 9,000 crore in dues
The world's tallest statue is unveiled in Gujarat
India bans TikTok and 58 other Chinese apps

title: Pharma Rollercoaster
story: A brutal stretch for Indian generic drugmakers as US drug prices fell and the US regulator cracked down on plants. Lupin lost half its value in eight years. Biocon's biosimilars took it up over 6x by 2021 before it fell back. Maruti Suzuki rose 2.5x.

headlines.text: The government launches a programme to put public services online
India's women cricketers reach the World Cup final at Lord's
Electronic toll tags become mandatory on national highways
India administers its 100-crore-th Covid vaccine dose

title: Power Play
story: Adani Enterprises rose about 25x in six years, crashed after the Hindenburg report in January 2023, and still ended about 43x. Tata Power and Genus Power multiplied in 2020-24 on renewables and smart meters. TCS compounded and then went flat.

headlines.text: Parliament passes a new law for resolving corporate insolvency
The Supreme Court decriminalises homosexuality
The Supreme Court grants women officers permanent commission in the Army
Air India returns to the Tata Group after 69 years

title: The Jio Effect
story: Reliance Jio launched in September 2016 with free calls and almost-free data. Idea merged with Vodafone, raised money again and again, and still lost 72% by 2024. Bharti Airtel survived and rose over 4x. Reliance rose 7x, raising money from Facebook and Google for Jio in 2020.

headlines.text: ISRO tests a scale model of a reusable space shuttle
The Supreme Court upholds Aadhaar but limits where it can be demanded
The IPL is played entirely in the UAE, in empty stadiums
India overtakes the UK to become the world's fifth-largest economy

title: Smallcap Fever
story: 2017 was a smallcap mania. Graphite India rose about 14x by mid-2018 as Chinese electrode plants shut, then lost most of it within a year. Vakrangee went from favourite to pariah when its auditor quit in 2018. IndiGo became India's dominant airline after Jet Airways collapsed in 2019, rising over 5x.

headlines.text: ISRO puts a record 104 satellites into orbit with a single rocket
A visa-free corridor opens for Indian pilgrims to a gurdwara in Pakistan
An Indian javelin thrower wins Olympic gold in athletics
India overtakes China as the world's most populous country

title: The Pandemic Pivot
story: Yes Bank lost 93% and had to be rescued by the RBI. Tanla, an obscure SMS company, rose about 45x in four years as OTPs and digital payments boomed, then gave back much of it. Deepak Nitrite rose 11x in the chemicals boom, and gold rose 5x.

headlines.text: A health insurance scheme covering 500 million people is launched
A new National Education Policy replaces the 1986 framework
India's largest insurer lists in the country's biggest IPO
An 18-year-old becomes the youngest undisputed world chess champion

title: The Defence Dividend
story: After the Galwan clash in 2020, India pushed hard to build its own weapons. Hindustan Aeronautics and Bharat Electronics rose 10-12x in eight years, and Cochin Shipyard rose about 15x in just two, 2022-24. Coal India, out of favour for years, more than doubled in the same stretch.

headlines.text: The Supreme Court allows women of all ages into the Sabarimala temple
Indian and Chinese troops clash in the Galwan Valley
India swears in its first tribal President
India wins the T20 World Cup in Barbados
